affine pullback, and supplies the canonical evaluation-divisor classifier.  The geometric input

field of `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`.

upstream obligation.  The endpoint here keeps that obligation in its geometric `IsPullback`
form and feeds the resulting arbitrary-scheme fibres immediately to
`picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented`.

Hence reading off the \u03a3-component\n191\trecovers `v` on the nose \u2014 no transport, no naturality.\n192\t\n193\tEverything in this section is this lemma read in one of two directions. -/\n194\tlemma sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero (m : \u2115) (Z : (C \u2297 overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)\n195\t    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z\n196\t      = (m : \u2124) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : \u2115) : \u2124))\n197\t    (T : Scheme.{u}) (v : T \u27f6 (Over.mk (\ud835\udfd9 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).left) :\n198\t    ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app (op T) v).1 = v := by\n199\t  change v \u226b \ud835\udfd9 _ = v\n200\t  rw [Category.comp_id]\n201\t\n202\tomit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in\n203\tvariable (C pi) in\n204\t/-- **ANTECEDENT 1'S ELEMENTWISE CONTENT IS UNCONDITIONAL AT THIS CHART**: the terminal chart\n205\tis injective on points at every test, with no hypothesis whatsoever.\n206\t\n207\tTwo points a lane must not misread.\n208\t\n209\t* This is **not** the `V = \u22a5` degeneracy of `isChartUniv_bot`\n210\t  (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat`). The\n218\t  fork's negative branch and this lemma live at different parameters, and the fork's own\n219\t  hypothesis `2 \u2264 Sheaf.h0` is what keeps them apart. -/\n220\ttheorem injective_abelSigmaChartZero (m : \u2115) (Z : (C \u2297 overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)\n221\t    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z\n222\t      = (m : \u2124) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : \u2115) : \u2124))\n223\t    (T : Scheme.{u}\u1d52\u1d56) :\n224\t    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T) := by\n225\t  intro v\u2081 v\u2082 h\n226\t  have h\u2081 := sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg T.unop v\u2081\n227\t  have h\u2082 := sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg T.unop v\u2082\n228\t  rw [\u2190 h\u2081, \u2190 h\u2082, h]\n229\t\n230\t/-! ## Surjectivity IS the vanishing\n231\t\n232\tThe \u03a3-component being the identity on points means the chart's app is surjective exactly when\n233\tthe fibre components are forced \u2014 and there is at most one thing to hit per structure\n234\tmorphism precisely when `pic\u2070` is a singleton there. Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the\n  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.\n* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` \u2014 the subgroup of classes of degree zero at\n  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).\n* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))\u1d52\u1d56 \u2964 CommGrpCat` \u2014 **the\n  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic\u2070_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup\n  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding\n  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design \u00a72.7).\n  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`\n  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion\n  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C \u27f6 picEtFunctor C`.\n-/\n\nset_option autoImplicit false\n\nuniverse u\n\nopen CategoryTheory\n\nnamespace AlgebraicGeometry\n\nvariable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}\n  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]\n\nnoncomputable section\n\n/-! ## The degree at a field point -/\n\n/-- **The degree of an \u00e9tale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along\n`t : overSpec k K \u27f6 T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test\nalgebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the\nrestricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/\ndef degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]\n    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K \u27f6 T) : \u2124 :=\n  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))\n\nsection DegAt\n\nvariable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]\n\n/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/\n@[simp]\ntheorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K \u27f6 T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by\n  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0\n  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]\n\n/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/\ntheorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K \u27f6 T) :\n    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by\n  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))\n      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))\n        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))\n  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]\n\n/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/\ntheorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K \u27f6 T) :\n    degAt lam\u207b\u00b9 t = -degAt lam t := by\n  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam\u207b\u00b9)) = -degAt lam t\n  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]\n  rfl\n\n/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a\nrestricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed\nfield point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting \u2014 this is what makes the stability of the\ndegree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/\ntheorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' \u27f6 T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K \u27f6 T') :\n    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' \u226b f) := by\n  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))\n      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' \u226b f) lam))\n  rw [\u2190 picEtMap_comp]\n\n/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/\ntheorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' \u27f6 T) (lam : picEt C T)\n    (t' : overSpec k K \u27f6 T') :\n    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' \u226b f) :=\n  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'\n\nend DegAt\n\n/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/\n\nvariable (C) in\n/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the \u00e9tale Picard group of a test object: the\nclasses of degree zero at every field point of the test. All rights reserved.\n     3\tReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\n     4\tAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n     5\t-/\n     6\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair\n     7\t\n     8\t/-!\n     9\t# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for\n    10\t\n    11\t`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` \u2014 the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that\n    12\t`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes \u2014 and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap\n    13\trow, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,\n    14\tCERT-\u03a3-gated.\n    15\t\n    16\t**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is\n    17\t`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and\n    18\t`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:\n    19\t\n    20\t1. **relative representability** \u2014 for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T \u27f6 \ud835\udcdf`, the\n    21\t   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;\n    22\t2. **the property clause** \u2014 every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.\n    23\t\n    24\tThe GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single\n    25\tpoint, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which\n    26\tis a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on\n    27\tCERT-\u03a3 for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with\n    28\tno divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.\n    29\t\n    30\t## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not\n    31\t\n    32\tEverything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves\n    33\t`f : yoneda.obj X \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V \u2286 X`.  No `divRep`\n    34\tendpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `\u03b8` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That\n    35\tis the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and\n    36\tthe divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.\n    37\t\n    38\tThe criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf \u2014 a fibrewise\n    39\tinjectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open \u2014 because that is what\n    40\tmathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf\n    41\tcategory's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).\n    42\t\n    43\t## Main declarations\n    44\t\n    45\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` \u2014 the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test\n    46\t  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points\n    47\t  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,\n    48\t  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.\n    49\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` \u2014 **the criterion**:\n    50\t  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses\n    51\t  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.\n    52\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` \u2014 the converse direction that makes\n    53\t  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So \"the\n    54\t  Abel map is not a monomorphism\", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted\n    55\t  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation \u2014 and\n    56\t  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of\n    57\t  this route.\n    58\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` \u2014 the same fact in the\n    59\t  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.\n    60\t-/\n    61\t\n    62\tset_option autoImplicit false\n    63\tset_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3\n    64\t\n    65\tuniverse u\n    66\t\n    67\topen CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory\n    68\t\n    69\tnamespace AlgebraicGeometry\n    70\t\n    71\tvariable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}\n    72\tvariable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]\n    73\tvariable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]\n    74\t\n    75\tnoncomputable section\n    76\t\n    77\t/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism\n    78\t\n    79\tStated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/\n    80\t\n    81\t/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**\n    82\t\n    83\tThis is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis\n    84\t`IsOpenImmersion \u2264 monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.\n    85\t\n    86\tRecorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence \"the Abel map is not a\n    87\tmonomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme\"\n    88\t(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a\n    89\t*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/\n    90\ttheorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}\n    91\t    {f : yoneda.obj X \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :\n    92\t    Mono f :=\n    93\t  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf\n    94\t\n    95\t/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of\n    96\tpresheaves then on every test it is injective on points.\n    97\t\n    98\tThis is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is\n    99\twhy that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of\n   100\t`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly \"the\n   101\tnormalized effective representative is unique\", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 \u2014 so\n   102\tGAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/\n   103\ttheorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}\n   104\t    {f : yoneda.obj X \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)\n   105\t    (T : Scheme.{u}\u1d52\u1d56) :\n   106\t    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=\n   107\t  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp\n   108\t    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)\n   109\t\n   110\t/-! ## The sufficient direction: the elementwise datum, and the criterion -/\n   111\t\n   112\tvariable (C) in\n   113\t/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**\n   114\t\n   115\tThis is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single\n   116\t`g : yoneda.obj T \u27f6 pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it\n   117\towes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:\n   118\t\n   119\t* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` \u2014 the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a\n   120\t  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;\n   121\t* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;\n   122\t* `sq` says the two ways round agree;\n   123\t* `exists_factor` is the honest content \u2014 a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with\n   124\t  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;\n   125\t  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.\u03b9` is a monomorphism.\n   126\t\n   127\tNothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart\n   128\tindex.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/\n   129\tstructure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}\n   130\t    (f : yoneda.obj X \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)\n   131\t    where\n   132\t  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/\n   133\t  W : T.Opens\n   134\t  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/\n   135\t  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) \u27f6 X\n   136\t  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/\n   137\t  sq : yoneda.map r \u226b f = yoneda.map W.\u03b9 \u226b g\n   138\t  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the\n   139\t  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/\n   140\t  exists_factor : \u2200 (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S \u27f6 X) (w : S \u27f6 T),\n   141\t    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w \u2192 \u2203 u : S \u27f6 (W : Scheme.{u}), u \u226b r = v \u2227 u \u226b W.\u03b9 = w\n   142\t\n   143\tnamespace ChartFibrePresented\n   144\t\n   145\tvariable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}\n   146\t  {g : yoneda.obj T \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}\n   147\t\n   148\t/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a\n   149\tpullback of presheaves.\n   150\t\n   151\tPullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise\n   152\t(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly\n   153\t\"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective\" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is\n   154\t`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.\u03b9` being a\n   155\tmonomorphism \u2014 which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/\n   156\ttheorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :\n   157\t    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.\u03b9) f g := by\n   158\t  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_\n   159\t  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]\n   160\t  refine \u27e8?_, ?_, ?_\u27e9\n   161\t  \u00b7 exact congrArg (fun \u03c6 : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>\n   162\t      \u03c6.app S) D.sq\n   163\t  \u00b7 -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.\u03b9` alone, being a monomorphism\n   164\t    rintro u\u2081 u\u2082 \u27e8-, h\u2082\u27e9\n   165\t    have : u\u2081 \u226b D.W.\u03b9 = u\u2082 \u226b D.W.\u03b9 := h\u2082\n   166\t    exact (cancel_mono D.W.\u03b9).mp this\n   167\t  \u00b7 -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`\n   168\t    intro v w hvw\n   169\t    obtain \u27e8u, hu\u2081, hu\u2082\u27e9 := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw\n   170\t    exact \u27e8u, hu\u2081, hu\u2082\u27e9\n   171\t\n   172\tend ChartFibrePresented\n   173\t\n   174\t/-- **THE CRITERION** \u2014 `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH\n   175\tclauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.\n   176\t\n   177\tGiven, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map\n   178\tis an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to\n   179\tdivisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on\n   180\teach.\n   181\t\n   182\tThis is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`\n   183\tas a single \"relative GAP-2\" statement conflates:\n   184\t\n   185\t* **relative representability** \u2014 that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here\n   186\t  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;\n   187\t* **the property clause** \u2014 that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied\n   188\t  here by `W.\u03b9` being an open immersion, which is free.\n   189\t\n   190\tWhat is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that\n   191\tagrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative\n   192\tform of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the\n   193\tclassifier \u2014 so the CERT-\u03a3 gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than\n   194\tthe whole certificate. -/\n   195\ttheorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}\n   196\t    (f : yoneda.obj X \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)\n   197\t    (D : \u2200 (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),\n   198\t      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :\n   199\t    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by\n   200\t  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_\n   201\t  exact \u27e8(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.\u03b9, (D T g).isPullback,\n   202\t    inferInstance\u27e9\n   203\t\n   204\t/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous\n   205\t\n   206\tA structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a\n   207\tcriterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather\n   208\tthan by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/\n   209\t\n   210\t/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**\n   211\t\n   212\tIf a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of\n   213\t`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied\n   214\tfor the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`\n   215\t(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the\n   216\tconclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.\n   217\t\n   218\tThe proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/\n   219\ttheorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}\n   220\t    (f : yoneda.obj X \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}\u1d52\u1d56)\n   221\t    (hT : \u00ac Function.Injective (f.app T)) :\n   222\t    IsEmpty (\u2200 (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' \u27f6 (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),\n   223\t        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=\n   224\t  \u27e8fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf\n   225\t    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)\u27e9\n   226\t\n   227\t/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**\n   228\telementwise injectivity on every test. All rights reserved.\nReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\nAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n-/\nimport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartVMonotone\nimport Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyBijective\n\n/-!\n# The two seam antecedents COLLAPSE at a one-chart atlas: the pair forces an ISOMORPHISM\n\nFour rows and three file headers in this project defer to one question, in these words:\n**\"inhabitation of the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` is unmeasured at every `V` and may be empty\neverywhere\"** (`AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict`, repeated verbatim on\n`\u2026datum.atlas-coupling`, whose own summary adds that its round \"removed a candidate escape from\nthat question, it did not answer it\").  Five files of endpoint refutations and monotonicity\nresults (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat`, `Pic0ChartVMonotone`, `Pic0ChartBotRefute`,\n`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling`, `Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj`) all stop there.\n\n**This file answers what the pair IS.**  For a one-chart atlas the two antecedents are not two\nindependent conditions to be met at some lucky `V` \u2014 together they say the chart map is an\n**isomorphism of sheaves onto `pic0SigmaSheaf C`**, and conversely any such isomorphism\nsatisfies both.  So the question \"is the pair inhabited at some `V`?\" is *equivalent* to\n\"is `pic0SigmaFunctor C` representable by an open of the divisor scheme?\", which is the\nproject's own headline restricted to a one-chart atlas.\n\n## Why this is a collapse and not a restatement\n\nThe two clauses are `MorphismProperty.relative`-shaped and sieve-shaped respectively, and\nnothing in the tree related them.  The bridge is that each is *half of a bijectivity*:\n\n* antecedent 1 (`IsChartUniv`, i.e. `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`) **implies** elementwise\n  injectivity on every test \u2014 that is `injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf`\n  (`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean`), which routes through\n  `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.  Injectivity on the nose is *stronger* than\n  `Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective`, so it gives it (`isLocallyInjective_of_injective`);\n* antecedent 2 is `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective` verbatim;\n* and mathlib's `Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso` turns locally-injective-plus-locally-\n  surjective into `IsIso` \u2014 **provided both sides are sheaves**.  The target is one by\n  construction (`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`); the source is one because the big Zariski topology\n  is **subcanonical** (`AlgebraicGeometry.subcanonical_zariskiTopology`, mathlib), so `yoneda.obj X`\n  is a sheaf for it with no hypothesis on `X` at all.\n\nThat last point is the step that had never been taken here: the chart source is representable,\nand on a subcanonical site a representable presheaf is a sheaf, so the seam's two antecedents\nlive in a category where mathlib's bijectivity criterion applies.  Nothing about `pic\u2070`,\ndivisors, charts or the curve enters any proof below.\n\n## What this buys, stated as three consequences and one non-consequence\n\n* **`chartIso_of_seam`** \u2014 the collapse. Both antecedents at a one-chart atlas give\n  `IsIso` of the sheaf morphism.\n* **`representableBy_of_seam`** \u2014 hence `pic0SigmaFunctor C` is represented by the chart\n  source *on the nose*, without going through mathlib's 01JJ gluing engine at all.  For a\n  one-chart atlas the whole `Scheme.LocalRepresentability` apparatus of\n  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is bypassed: the glued scheme is the chart.\n* **`exists_retraction_of_seam`** \u2014 the sharp constraint on `V`.  If the pair holds at `V` then\n  the open inclusion `V.\u03b9 : \u21a5V \u27f6 D.left` is a **split mono in `Scheme`**: the chart map\n  composed with the inverse retracts it.  So a working `V` is not merely a proper intermediate\n  open (which is all the endpoint results gave); it is a **retract of the divisor scheme**.\n  That is a much stronger structural demand, and it is the form in which the inhabitation\n  question should be attacked next.\n* **The non-consequence, and it is why this file does not claim to have answered the question.**\n  `IsIso` is an *equivalent reformulation*, not a refutation and not a witness.  Nothing below\n  exhibits a `V` at which the pair holds, and nothing below refutes one.  What changes is that\n  the target is now a single familiar statement about one morphism instead of a conjunction of\n  two conditions of different shapes \u2014 and that the retraction constraint is available to\n  whoever attacks it.\n\n## Scope: one chart, and that is a real restriction\n\nEvery statement here is for a **`PUnit`-indexed** atlas.  That is not a convenience: for a\ngeneral `\u03b9` the two antecedents are about *different* morphisms (`f i` versus `Sigma.desc f`),\nand `Sigma.desc f` is not a map out of a representable, so `chartSheafHom` cannot even be\n*formed* on it: the collapse needs the **source** to be a sheaf, and a coproduct of\nrepresentables is not one in general \u2014 subcanonicity gives the sheaf property of\n`yoneda.obj X`, not of `\u2210 i, yoneda.obj (X i)`.  (Measured rather than asserted: an `exact?`\non `Presheaf.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (\u2210 fun i => yoneda.obj (X i))` finds nothing, which\nis weak evidence of absence on a composite goal but is the right *reason* \u2014 the coproduct\npresheaf is a sheaf only after sheafification, and that is a different object from the one the\nseam's antecedent 2 is stated about.)\n\nThe one-chart case is not a caricature either \u2014 `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds a\none-chart atlas, and `IsChartUniv`, `RestrictedChartFibre` and `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff`\nare all stated for one.  But a lane must not read `chartIso_of_seam` as a statement about\n`mixedParamChart` at arbitrary `\u03b9`.  `isLocallySurjective_oneChart` below is the bridge that\nmakes the one-chart hypothesis usable in the coproduct spelling the seam consumes, so the\nrestriction is to the *index*, not to the *spelling*.\n\n## Main declarations\n\n* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartSourceSheaf` \u2014 the chart source as a sheaf, by subcanonicity.\n* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_oneChart` \u2014 antecedent 2 in the coproduct spelling\n  gives local surjectivity of the single chart.\n* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartIso_of_seam` \u2014 **the collapse**.\n* `AlgebraicGeometry.seam_of_chartIso` \u2014 **the converse**, so this is an equivalence and not a\n  weakening.\n* Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files\nby hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or\nfields.\n\n## Read\n\n- `horizon inbox list` \u2014 read the inbox. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale\n  memories, and consumed notices. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which\n  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for\n  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:\n  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids\n  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is\n  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.\n- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,\n  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /\n  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). It should ignore other\n  projects' and other teams' addressed items.\n- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The\n  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every\n  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:\n  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.\n- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),\n  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),\n  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the\n  human \u2014 something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project\n  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),\n  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).\n\n## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)\n\nEach running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams.
